title: Consolidate CI toolchains, implement remote build-cache proxy, and optimize build graph
creator: Aisha Ramos
description: Problem: CI run times and flakiness have regressed as we added more matrix jobs, custom per-repo toolchain installs, and ad-hoc cache keys. This increases cost, slows developer feedback loops, and makes rollbacks riskier. Goal: Reduce median full-check CI time by ~40%, cut per-pipeline egress/storage costs by 30%, and eliminate >90% of flaky toolchain installs across the fleet. Scope: centralize language/toolchain installs into curated images and a small set of maintained runtime images; introduce a slim remote build-cache proxy (ccache/sccache/remote-ccache) for shared object artifacts and Node/Yarn cache layers; collapse redundant matrix axes by moving cross-platform compile checks to scheduled jobs; and refactor workspace build graph to enable parallelism for independent modules. Non-goals: replace underlying runner provider, migrate to Bazel, or change release gating rules in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Median full-check CI time reduced >= 35% on representative repos (api, runtime, console)
Remote build cache hit rate >= 80% within 2 weeks of rollout for warmed repos
Docker base images standardized to 4 curated variants (linux-x64, linux-arm64, slim, build) with documented upgrade process
All repos using centralized toolchain images or opt-in scripts; <5 repos remain on ad-hoc installs
Exhaustive runbook created: rollback steps, cache invalidation, and migration checklist
No regressions in integration E2E test pass rate (>= previous baseline)
Security review completed for remote cache proxy and image signing
migration_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): Build and publish 4 curated base images; onboard 3 low-risk repos for validation
Phase 2 (3 weeks): Deploy remote build-cache proxy (k8s service behind internal LB) and enable sccache for Rust/Go artifacts
Phase 3 (2 weeks): Enable Node/Yarn remote layer caching and move runners to mount cache proxy; collapse matrix axes where safe
Phase 4 (2 weeks): Bulk migration of remaining repos, monitoring heatmap and fallback toggles; documentation and training
Rollback Plan: Pin pipelines to previous images and disable cache proxy (toggle in CI infra); invalidate caches via admin endpoint
metrics: Target: median CI run time (full-check) from baseline 22m -> <= 14m
Target: build-cache hit rate >= 80% on warm repos
Target: average Docker image size reduction of 25-35% for build images
Target: per-pipeline bandwidth/storage spend down by >= 30% month-over-month after rollout
risks: Cache poisoning or stale artifacts causing hard-to-detect regressions; mitigated by short TTLs and signed cache entries
Security exposure from remote cache; require mTLS + ACLs and security review
Hard-to-migrate repos with native binaries or unusual OS deps; keep opt-out path and manual migration support
Initial flakiness when switching images (diff in glibc/openssl); smoke test gate before rollouts
